summary_en: This study tests 27T51, an experimental CAR T cell therapy that targets the MUC16 protein, in adults with recurrent or hard-to-treat epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer. 27T51 is given by intravenous (IV) infusion, alone or with cemiplimab and bevacizumab, which are also given by IV infusion; how often and for how long is not stated. The record does not state a main outcome measure; it is a Phase 1 study with stated aims of testing safety and finding the highest dose without unacceptable side effects.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa 27T51, una terapia experimental con células CAR T que actúa contra la proteína MUC16, en adultos con cáncer de ovario epitelial, carcinoma peritoneal primario o cáncer de trompa de Falopio recurrente o difícil de tratar. El 27T51 se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV), solo o con cemiplimab y bevacizumab, que también se administran por infusión IV; la frecuencia y la duración no están indicadas. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; es un estudio de Fase 1 con objetivos declarados de evaluar la seguridad y encontrar la dosis más alta sin efectos secundarios inaceptables.
who_for: ECOG performance status of 1 or lower
Histological diagnosis of epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer
Recurrent or refractory disease, as described in the protocol
Serum CA-125 at least 2 times the upper limit of normal
At least one measurable tumor lesion by RECIST 1.1 and expected survival of at least 3 months
not_for: Inadequate heart, kidney, or liver function, as described in the protocol
Absolute lymphocyte count below 100 cells/μL at time of leukapheresis
Grade 2 or higher hemorrhage within 30 days, or inadequate coagulation parameters
Clinically relevant central nervous system pathology, as described in the protocol
Significant autoimmune disease needing systemic immunosuppression within 2 years, or prior cellular or gene therapy
